stem.text: Water flows into a tank at a rate of \( R(t) \) liters per minute, where \( R \) is a differentiable function of time \( t \) in minutes. Selected values of \( R(t) \) are given in the table. At time \( t = 0 \) the tank holds 40 liters of water. \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccc} t & 0 & 2 & 5 & 9 & 10 \\ \hline R(t) & 12 & 16 & 10 & 8 & 14 \end{array} \]

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table to approximate \( \displaystyle\int_{0}^{10} R(t)\,dt \). Show the computations that lead to your answer.

worked_solution.text: One trapezoid per subinterval, width times the average of the endpoint values.

points.criterion: Writes a trapezoidal sum over the four subintervals with each width and each pair of endpoint values shown.
Gives the value 114 supported by that sum.

parts.prompt: Use your answer from part (a) to approximate the amount of water in the tank at time \( t = 10 \).

points.criterion: Adds the initial 40 liters to the integral of R from 0 to 10 (or its approximation) to estimate the amount at t = 10.

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the two subintervals indicated by the table on \( 2 \le t \le 9 \) to approximate the average rate of flow into the tank over that interval.

worked_solution.text: Divide by the length of the interval.

points.criterion: Writes the two-trapezoid sum on [2, 9] and divides by the interval length 7.
